title: Your trading journal
desc: Log six fields for every trade and find your patterns each week

cards.title: “I’m doing OK”
cards.situation: You’ve made 40 trades in two months and written nothing down. You feel you’re doing OK. What can’t you tell without a record?

visual.title: 40 trades · no notes
visual.label: An account line that wanders up and down and ends a little lower

options.feedback: Everyone’s memory keeps the big wins and quietly drops the small losses. Only a record shows what really works.

options.text: Which setups make money and which lose it
options.feedback: Without notes you can’t see which trades to repeat and which to stop.
Your broker already counts your trades. What it can’t tell you is why each one won or lost.

cards.work: Your broker shows 22 wins and 18 losses, net −$140. Your memory said “doing OK”.

cards.title: Six things to log
cards.text: A **[[trading-journal|trading journal]]** is a short note for every trade. The same six fields each time, written the same day.

blocks.tip: The emotion line matters as much as the numbers. It shows why a trade went wrong.

cards.title: The weekly review
cards.text: Every weekend, you sort the week’s trades by emotion.

items.label: Five trades this week, each with its emotion and result

blocks.tip: One pattern found: the off-plan trades cost the week.

cards.title: Log daily, review weekly
cards.text: A journal you never read is just a diary. The **[[weekly-review|weekly review]]** is where it pays.

items.title: Log every trade the same day
items.text: All six fields, wins and losses alike.

items.title: Every weekend, look for one pattern
items.text: Keep what works. Cut one thing that doesn’t.

cards.title: On plan or not?
cards.q: Here’s your entry for trade #42. Was the −$2 loss on plan?

options.feedback: Easy to miss: small isn’t the test. The stop set the plan. Losing more means the stop was moved or ignored.

options.text: No: you lost more than planned
options.feedback: The stop capped the plan at about $1.40 a share. Losing $2 means it was moved or ignored, and “Rushed” hints why.
The target doesn’t decide this. Compare the loss with the distance from entry to stop.

options.text: You can’t tell from this entry
options.feedback: The entry has what you need: entry, stop and result. Compare the loss with the risk you planned.

cards.title: Why the feelings?
cards.q: Why should you log your emotion as well as the numbers?

options.text: It makes the journal look complete
options.feedback: It isn’t for looks. The emotion line is where your losing patterns show up.

options.text: It shows which feelings lead to your losing trades
options.feedback: The numbers show what happened. The emotion shows why, and that’s the part you can change.
Your broker never sees your journal. It’s for you, to find the feelings behind your trades.

options.text: Emotions don’t matter if the numbers are right
options.feedback: The numbers show what happened. The emotion shows why, and that’s the part you can change.

cards.headline: You can learn from every trade you make.
lines: Log setup, entry, stop, target, result and emotion.
Write it the same day, wins and losses alike.
Review weekly and fix one pattern at a time.
